reviews.rationale: Microsoft's own preview FAQ, preserved at the time and within the target window, says Recall did not moderate content or hide sensitive data such as passwords. Its exclusions were user-chosen or tied to specific apps, not automatic recognition of sensitive content. This meets the support condition. Health information was not tested separately, but the general admission covers it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own firm statement in the post.

semantics.note: 'Is not going to' is a firm forecast with no deadline. The normalised version keeps both denials, and the concession about AI in general is correctly not treated as a condition.

contract.note: Reading 'change the world' as major societal or economic transformation is an ordinary, fair reading. With no deadline, the denial can only be resolved early, by contradicting evidence.

evidence.note: St. Louis Fed: reported time savings of 1.6% and a model-based productivity gain of up to 1.3%. The authors caution against reading causation into it, so this is not established transformation.
NPR on an OpenAI proof checked in Lean. It is a notable advance, but its wider societal or economic impact is not shown.
Randomised trial in which AI slowed experienced developers by 19%. It covers a narrow setting and cannot prove that no transformation will ever happen.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, so the claim can only be resolved early, by an independently confirmed major transformation. The packet shows growing adoption, modest productivity estimates, one disputed mathematical advance and a negative trial. None of it establishes a broad transformation tied to generative AI, OpenAI or Anthropic, and an open-ended denial cannot be confirmed either.
